method: All 70 dated feature records were examined under the existing scoring rubric. Existing scores are retained; evidence gaps are named rather than treated as fresh failures or passes. No activity entry grants readiness credit and no new owner acceptance is added.

features.summary: Historical cold starts and five-tab observations support the existing device and real-world checks. On Nov 2, unpublished tester69 reopened existing signed-in accounts after two in-place updates. Those limited install/session checks do not clear warm-pairing or certificate issues, or establish acceptance of the public tester68 download.

On Nov 2, Galaxy S24 tester67 restarted near the beginning after five of five converted-stream jump/switch attempts. Later tests also failed two of three Original-quality far jumps, while three converted-720p jumps held; the cause remains unproven. On tester68, now the public download, nine S9+ far jumps passed on a test server; the S24 was not retried. Four bounded S9+ seek/reveal observations passed on unpublished tester69. Its touch guard is absent from the public tester68 build and does not prove the S24 failure fixed. A tester68 audio-delay attempt selected -250 ms instead of the intended -500 ms: inconclusive, with four remaining selections not run and sound not judged. The distinct snap-back failure raises known issues from four to five; the existing cap keeps this row at 90%.

Real mobile-data playback and network switching support the historical real-world mark. Browser Auto/480p and reconnect limitations remain. Source repairs do not establish current route or playback acceptance.

Two-phone host/viewer playback, seek and pause support the device mark. Observed delays and the cloud-room join limitation remain; a later non-reproduction does not prove general closure or real-world acceptance.

The historical two-phone host-code, QR, join and leave check supports the device mark. Later identity blockage prevented a newer-build pass. The current note is qualified so it does not erase the older test; real-world acceptance remains open.

Retains Nick's Oct 26 feature-specific acceptance of the matching Library Health counts. Missing-episode fixtures, Fix/Open, recovery and subsequent Open implementation remain outside that scoped approval.

Retains the feature-specific Oct 27 owner/coordinator acceptance of random playback, controls, saved marks and playlist operations with heard sound. Empty/error, sharing, smart-list and TV-show cases remain outside scope.
Two-phone local hosting, downloaded playback and later lobby/join/leave/Stop checks support the retained score. Two issues and mobile-data, hotspot and unmatched-stop cases remain.

Retains the scoped Oct 27 acceptance based on real listening and the Follow-label retest. Later desktop work does not extend Android acceptance; newer queue, download, recording and sleep cases remain separate.

Historical chapter, speed, bookmark and owner-heard playback checks remain. On Nov 2, tester68, now the public download, held the saved place in 14 of 15 book-to-film attempts; one ended about 27 seconds ahead, with the cause unresolved (FAIL-INCONCLUSIVE). Two further tester68 checks and one on unpublished tester69 did not reproduce it, but do not clear that result. Sound was not judged in these newer checks. The existing account/book-removal issue also remains open.

Retry/estimate tests and real offline original/compressed playback support the historical checks. The blank notification entry and low-space, cancellation and process-durability limits remain. Source promotion tests add no device credit.
Real-phone export completion supports the device mark. A second-phone timeout and photos-plus-clip failure remain. Finished-file playback and a real outing/privacy journey still lack acceptance.
Game-rule tests and two-phone natural match finishes support the historical checks. Three issues remain; bounded later native-game observations do not establish acceptance for every game.

Two-phone photo navigation, a saved-video hash match and picture checks support the device mark. Newer video-policy tests add source evidence only. Audible playback and concurrency remain unproved. The Nov 2 automated checks used unpublished tester69 source; they do not validate the public tester68 download.
Real browser outputs and audio-node/stop/restart checks support device-level behavior. The checks were muted, so audible synchronization and timing remain unproved; no real-world mark is added.

A second phone installed over its existing same-version app and APK identity checks passed. That supports the historical device mark. A fresh never-installed device and actual expiry remain untested; the old summary is narrowed accordingly.
The real-phone button/result and screen observations support only the existing device UI mark. No demonstrated wake of a sleeping PC is recorded; real-world acceptance remains open.

Historical casting checks remain. On Nov 2, Nick confirmed picture, sound and controls on tester67. A later phone-position reset followed an uncertain tap; an app defect was not established. Tester68, now the public download, passed one short converted-cast hand-back check without sound judgment. The cited unpublished tester69 receipt contains no cast test. Six existing issues and stuck, direct-stream, end, next-episode and broader TV cases remain open.

Nick's own-car use, tabs, progress and heard episode audio support historical real-world credit. The explicit 90% cap remains for the thin car record, phone-settings issue and untested driving, passenger, resume and other-car cases.

Navigation, directional-pad and focus unit suites passed on Nov 2 against the source used for unpublished tester69. These are automated source checks, not validation of the public tester68 download. Real Android TV and Fire TV acceptance remains unproved.

A sideloaded phone demo played its sample clips and exited. The device mark is limited to that demo, not Google Play distribution. Closed-test submission, distribution and real-world acceptance remain unproved.

Session, isolation and one-shot automated suites passed, while the feature remains gated and absent from the observed menus. Only automated credit is retained; no exposed end-to-end feature or receiver acceptance is recorded. The Nov 2 automated checks used unpublished tester69 source; they do not validate the public tester68 download.
The old separate feature was absent from menus and retired into Remote Desktop. All checks remain false and the score remains 0%.
Link, renewal, revocation and retry source tests are recorded. A phone or scripted receiver is not real-TV acceptance, so device and real-world marks remain false.

Owner-confirmed large text/contrast and later maximum-font fixes support the existing 99%. Complete accessibility workflows and TalkBack judged by ear remain open, and final acceptance stays false. Desktop-only fixes add no Android credit.

Retains Nick's Oct 26 feature-specific acceptance of phone music playback with heard audio. Newer queue and timer suites are source evidence only. Gapless/crossfade, mixes and casting remain outside the accepted subset. The Nov 2 automated checks used unpublished tester69 source; they do not validate the public tester68 download.
Retains Nick's Oct 26 scoped acceptance of the tested family jobs, stars and dashboard controls. This does not establish long-running family use or broader multi-phone behavior.

Retains Nick's Oct 26 scoped local add/tick/delete acceptance and the historical sync checks. Newer checklist tests do not establish a real trip, which remains untested. The Nov 2 automated checks used unpublished tester69 source; they do not validate the public tester68 download.

Retains Nick's Oct 26 scoped recipe scaling, editing, privacy and delete/undo acceptance. Newer recipe/shopping suites add source evidence only; outgoing Share/Copy remains outside the approved subset. The Nov 2 automated checks used unpublished tester69 source; they do not validate the public tester68 download.

Retains Nick's Oct 26 scoped collections/request acceptance. A later same-day trailer picture/sound observation is already recorded and supersedes the old 'untried' note. Newer collection tests do not broaden final acceptance. The Nov 2 automated checks used unpublished tester69 source; they do not validate the public tester68 download.

Narrow backup, hash, counter and photo/video observations coexist with three recorded failures. Location, native-backup and missing-root gaps still prevent broad device and real-world marks. One file or counter increment does not close them.

Real milestone, duplicate/reopen/cancel and owner/member checks support the device mark; newer rules/store suites support automation. Actual retention intervals and sustained family use remain unproved. The Nov 2 automated checks used unpublished tester69 source; they do not validate the public tester68 download.

Installed download, integrity verification, update to Windows 0.1.109 and reopening support the existing device and real-world record. The explicit 90% cap remains; low disk, uninstall, active viewing and other PCs still need checks.

Installed library and player checks, a muted hour-long run and later source checks support the retained mark. Six recorded issues, sound, broader browsers and player journeys remain. A newer browser sign-in pass does not complete the player.
Automatic and Ask-me updates ran on the installed PC. Download-only, Tonight, active viewing and an observed real restart remain unproved; the real-world check stays open.

Historical transcoding and installed-PC checks support the retained device mark. On Nov 2, checks using Android tester67 with Windows 0.1.110 passed three converted-720p far jumps, but other sound-setting and Original-playback cases reset the position. The cause remains unproven. These mixed results do not clear the two existing converter issues: wasted starts and the recorded browser failure. Broader GPU and format checks remain.
HTTP and restriction checks plus installed playback of a two-channel test playlist support the recorded checks. A real tuner/provider, guide, recording, Live TV casting and listening remain open.

The installed painted preview, draft and short export passed. Later title and scene fixes have source checks but still need an installed retest. Voiced export, captions, saving and household-profile review remain.

Room, vote and filtering checks and partial browser/desktop journeys support implementation and automated marks. The complete installed multi-device journey remains partial, with four open issues and no new device or real-world credit.
Protocol, range, membership and logout checks passed. The actual third-party client failed playback and triggered unwanted conversion; successful API checks do not close either client acceptance gap.

Installed rating, profile and timed-cutoff checks support the device mark. Short-limit and mid-film restriction findings, phone/TV screens and broader household scenarios remain open. New source tests do not clear them.
Installed keyboard and Settings checks support the device mark. A real Windows screen reader, forced colours and broader focus paths remain; the newer visual preview is not screen-reader acceptance.

Browser fit and installed language/table inspections support the device mark. English leftovers, fit problems, native-speaker review and right-to-left coverage remain. Build/report work does not establish translation quality.

Retains Nick's existing, feature-specific acceptance of desktop posters and information on Windows 0.1.104, including the five-title and missing-poster checks. This does not extend acceptance to other builds, offline behavior or TV artwork.

Historical implementation and passing safety tests are recorded, but a detailed dated execution packet could not be located in this review. The existing 49% is retained with that provenance gap. Real-PC viewing, control, approval and revocation remain untested.

Upload integrity, a real-phone backup and later photo transfer/scan checks support the device mark. The later copy-integrity difference remains open; full-folder removal, restore, conflicts, low space and NAS behavior are unproved.

The historical two-household invite, shared playback and revocation checks support the existing real-world mark. Three issues remain, and newer share-code repairs still need complete two-household acceptance. Source defaults are not live configuration proof.

Strong-mode media output has automated coverage, but no matching listening acceptance is recorded. Night and Basic mode checks do not test Strong. Device and real-world marks stay false pending sound, clipping, pumping and sync checks.

The PC/two-phone record and later real browser-guest playback support the existing device mark. Recent checks were muted; acoustic alignment, calibration, surround, Bluetooth and physical output remain unproved.

The installed music player and sleep timer ran in muted checks; later browser Repeat, Queue and Lyrics empty-state checks are recorded. Real lyrics, listening, gapless/crossfade and the mix-before-rescan issue remain. The obsolete 'desktop not launched' note is corrected.

Installed layout save, persistence, reset and row/pack checks support the retained real-world mark. Three recorded issues remain. Newer immediate pack saving is observed, with its intended behavior still unresolved.

The Windows 0.1.109 wall, Last-used and open-page removal checks support the existing device mark. That frame was created through the API, not the Settings wizard; the record is corrected. Phone/tablet/TV, expiry, presence and current setup acceptance remain.

Browser banner checks and installed sender/history tests are recorded. Native-phone delivery failed and the earlier Enable issue is not conclusively closed. The obsolete 'sender untested' summary is corrected; receiver, limits and audible Listen acceptance remain.

Actual Docker execution on a Windows PC under WSL2 passed source and container smokes, transcoding and restart persistence. This supports the historical Docker-on-PC device mark, not native Linux desktop, ARM, NAS or hardware-accelerated container acceptance.

Linux packages built and launched in the recorded WSLg environment with special launch options. Native desktop use, normal launch, media, tray, GPU, package mounting and updates remain untested; no device or real-world credit is added.

Source implementation and Windows-only platform checks are recorded. A claimed completed Mac package could not be substantiated: the located build stopped before packaging. The 49% is retained for source work with an evidence gap; no verified Mac artifact or native acceptance is claimed.

The public DNS, TLS and HTTP checks support the limited historical device and real-world marks. The explicit 90% cap remains for unfinished migration and whole-feature gaps; deployment identity and administrative completion are not established.

Actual away playback, sound and reconnect records support historical device and real-world checks. Both open issues remain. New source work does not prove the installed repair, route selection, renewal or concurrent-user behavior.

Retains the existing feature-specific owner acceptance and its recorded coordinator disposition for the tested website/browser games. It does not cover every browser or game mode, newer native games, or the new feature-page publication checks.

Historical source tests cover rate limits, expiry and link handling, but the original execution receipt was not recovered. The 49% is retained with that evidence gap. Actual email delivery and recovery, provider readiness and current deployment remain unproved.

Engine and connection work has historical test claims, but the precise execution receipt was not recovered. The 49% is retained with that gap. Real players, reconnection, moderation and current runtime availability remain unproved; static browser games are separate.

The replacement calling flow has source/review history, but its original automated execution receipt was not independently recovered. Older device credit was withdrawn; opening the newer phone sheet did not join a call or prove audio. The existing 49% remains provisional.

The dated record confirms source gates and default-disabled behavior, not an underlying executed test packet or live reachability. Retain Planned and the historical 49% with that evidence gap; device and real-world checks remain absent.

A real phone opened the photo/clip link over mobile data in the historical tested build. That supports the device mark only. The current route, another person or iPhone, expiry, revocation and an offline host remain unproved.

Earlier successful Windows use remains a historical owner report; its exact artifact and original dated receipt are not established. On Nov 2, automated checks reproduced a configuration-validation failure in source. A proposed source repair passed its checks, but no repaired installed VPN artifact or native tunnel was tested. This is one known source issue, not ten separate issues or a claim about the installed app. The Oct 30 away-access failure also remains unresolved. Retain the 55% cap; routes, DNS and recovery remain unverified.

Fraud, ledger, wallet and callback source tests are recorded. Disabled source defaults do not prove current deployed configuration. No device, real-world, payment activation or availability credit is added.
Planning is recorded, without completed implementation, provisioning, backup, monitoring or operational acceptance. No evidence supports moving the score above 0%.
Planning is recorded, without an accepted hosting control, backup or incident workflow. No evidence supports moving the score above 0%.
The placeholder/framework and paused roadmap are not a finished integration or end-to-end result. No evidence supports moving the score above 0%.
Roadmap and example home-automation setup are not a demonstrated Google Assistant or Alexa integration. No real setup or command acceptance supports moving above 0%.
